title: Calico dataplane
description: Calico CNI and NetworkPolicy: Felix sync/programming latency/iptables errors, Typha streams, IPAM pool usage, tigera-operator status. Curated for this lab; see docs/dashboards/networking.md.

list.name: Felix datastore resync
list.textFormat: Felix on {{pod}} started a full datastore resync

panels.title: How to read this dashboard
panels.description: Reading guide for this dashboard.

options.content:
**What this is.** Calico is the cluster network (CNI) and NetworkPolicy engine, installed by Ansible through the **tigera-operator**.
- **Felix** (in `calico-node`, hostNetwork) programs the node: pod routes, **iptables** rules and ipsets for every NetworkPolicy
  (dataplane mode iptables; eBPF and nftables are off).
- **Typha** fans out datastore updates from the Kubernetes API to Felix.
- **calico-kube-controllers** does IPAM garbage collection and syncs Kubernetes objects; it exports the **IP pool** usage.
- **tigera-operator** reconciles all of the above (and goldmane/whisker flow logs, webhooks, apiserver).

**Healthy looks like:** Felix *in sync* (state 3), dataplane failures not increasing, iptables/ipset errors 0, dataplane apply p99
well under 1 s, Typha streaming to calico-node, IP pool far from full, all operator components Available.

**When something goes red:** Felix not in sync or failures growing → `kubectl --context k8s01 -n calico-system logs ds/calico-node`;
operator component degraded → `kubectl --context k8s01 get tigerastatus`; pool nearly full → add an IPPool (Ansible).
Alerts: `helm-charts/monitoring/monitoring-raw/calico.rules.yaml`. Official Felix/Typha dashboards sit next to this one. Details: `docs/dashboards/networking.md`.

panels.title: Active alerts for this service
panels.description: Prometheus alerts of this service that are FIRING (condition true for longer than the rule's `for`) or PENDING (condition true, waiting for `for`). Same filter as the red alert annotations of this dashboard; Watchdog/InfoInhibitor are excluded. Empty = healthy. Alertmanager has no receiver in this lab, so dashboards are where alerts are seen: the rule, its threshold and source are in the rule files (helm-charts/<app>/**/prometheus.rules.yaml or the -raw release) and in docs/dashboards/. All alerts of the lab: dashboard "Alerts overview" (Observability folder).

panels.title: Felix state
panels.description: felix_resync_state (https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/felix/prometheus): 1 = waiting for datastore, 2 = resync in progress, 3 = in sync. Anything other than 3 for 15 min fires CalicoFelixNotInSync (helm-charts/monitoring/monitoring-raw/calico.rules.yaml): policy and routes may be stale.

panels.title: Dataplane failures (range)
panels.description: Failed dataplane programming attempts in the time range (felix_int_dataplane_failures, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/felix/prometheus). Felix retries; isolated failures right after boot/rollout are normal, a steady increase fires CalicoFelixDataplaneFailures (helm-charts/monitoring/monitoring-raw/calico.rules.yaml).

panels.title: iptables/ipset errors (range)
panels.description: Errors of the iptables-restore, iptables-save and ipset subprocesses in the time range (felix_iptables_restore_errors, felix_iptables_save_errors, felix_ipset_errors, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/felix/prometheus; 'Dataplane subprocess errors' of the official dashboard https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/v3.33.0/manifests/grafana-dashboards.yaml). Must be 0; restore errors fire CalicoFelixIptablesRestoreErrors.

panels.title: Typha → Felix streams
panels.description: calico-node Felix clients streaming from Typha (typha_connections_streaming, syncer felix, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/typha/prometheus). 0 fires CalicoTyphaNoStreamingClients: Felix gets no updates.

panels.title: IP pool used
panels.description: Pod IPs allocated / IP pool size (ipam_allocations_in_use / ipam_ippool_size, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/kube-controllers/prometheus). Alert CalicoIPPoolNearlyFull at 90% (helm-charts/monitoring/monitoring-raw/calico.rules.yaml).

panels.title: Operator components degraded
panels.description: tigera-operator components reporting Degraded (tigera_operator_component_status, mirrors TigeraStatus https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/installation/api). Fires TigeraOperatorComponentDegraded after 15 min.

panels.title: Dataplane apply time (p50/p90/p99)
panels.description: How long Felix takes to apply a batch of changes to iptables/ipsets/routes (felix_int_dataplane_apply_time_seconds summary, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/felix/prometheus; '99%ile dataplane update time' of https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/v3.33.0/manifests/grafana-dashboards.yaml). This is the closest metric to *policy programming latency*: after a NetworkPolicy or pod change, the node enforces it this long later (plus calc graph time). Healthy: tens of ms; seconds = iptables lock contention or a huge ruleset.

panels.title: Calculation graph update time p99
panels.description: Time Felix's calculation graph spends processing one datastore update before it reaches the dataplane (felix_calc_graph_update_time_seconds, quantile 0.99, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/felix/prometheus; '99%ile calculation update time' of https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/v3.33.0/manifests/grafana-dashboards.yaml).

panels.title: Dataplane operations & failures
panels.description: Dataplane apply operations per minute (rate of felix_int_dataplane_apply_time_seconds_count ×60, https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/v3.33.0/manifests/grafana-dashboards.yaml) and failed attempts (increase of felix_int_dataplane_failures). Operations follow pod/policy churn; failures should be flat.

panels.title: iptables / ipset subprocess errors
panels.description: Per-second errors of iptables-restore, iptables-save and ipset (https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/felix/prometheus; same sum as 'Dataplane subprocess errors' in https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/v3.33.0/manifests/grafana-dashboards.yaml). 0 normally; errors usually come from another program (kube-proxy, Docker, ufw) fighting over iptables or a kernel module missing.

panels.title: iptables rules & ipsets
panels.description: Rules Felix programmed per iptables table and ipsets it owns (felix_iptables_rules, felix_ipsets_calico, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/felix/prometheus; 'Iptables rules'/'IP sets' of https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/v3.33.0/manifests/grafana-dashboards.yaml). Grows with policies × endpoints; a jump without a policy change = runaway selector.

panels.title: Active endpoints, policies, selectors
panels.description: Pods (workload endpoints), policies and selectors active on this node (felix_active_local_endpoints/_policies/_selectors, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/felix/prometheus). Explains why the ruleset and apply time grow.

panels.title: Felix errors logged & resyncs
panels.description: Error-level log lines Felix wrote (rate of felix_log_errors) and full datastore resyncs started (changes of felix_resyncs_started, as in 'Felix datastore resyncs/hr' of https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/v3.33.0/manifests/grafana-dashboards.yaml). Error logs without failures are often transient (e.g. a pod deleted mid-update); check calico-node logs when they persist.

panels.title: Route table resync time
panels.description: Time Felix needs to resync the node's routing tables (felix_route_table_resync_seconds summary p99, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/felix/prometheus). Slow resyncs delay new pod reachability.

panels.title: calico-node memory & CPU
panels.description: Working-set memory and CPU cores of the calico-node container (cAdvisor).

panels.title: Streaming connections by syncer
panels.description: Clients streaming from Typha per syncer (typha_connections_streaming, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/typha/prometheus): felix (policy/routes), node-status, tunnel-ip-allocation (calico-node), bgp (unused: no BGP here).

panels.title: Client fall-behind & ping latency (p99)
panels.description: How far behind clients are at reading updates (typha_client_latency_secs) and the round-trip of Typha pings (typha_ping_latency), quantile 0.99 (https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/typha/prometheus; same panels in the official Typha dashboard https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/blob/v3.33.0/manifests/grafana-dashboards.yaml). Seconds = Felix overloaded or the node starved.

panels.title: Connections accepted / dropped
panels.description: New client connections and connections Typha dropped (typha_connections_accepted / _dropped, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/typha/prometheus). Steady accepts = clients reconnecting in a loop.

panels.title: IP allocations vs pool size
panels.description: Pod IPs in use per pool and the pool size (ipam_allocations_in_use, ipam_ippool_size, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/kube-controllers/prometheus). The default pool 10.244.0.0/16 has 65 536 addresses.

panels.title: IPAM blocks & borrowed IPs
panels.description: Address blocks (/26 by default) assigned to the node and IPs borrowed from another node's block (ipam_blocks_per_node, ipam_allocations_borrowed, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/kube-controllers/prometheus). Single node: borrowed should stay 0.

panels.title: Leaked IP candidates
panels.description: Allocations kube-controllers considers leaked (no matching pod) and will garbage-collect (ipam_allocations_gc_candidates, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/kube-controllers/prometheus). Non-zero for long = IPAM GC stuck (check calico-kube-controllers logs).

panels.title: Component status
panels.description: TigeraStatus conditions per component (tigera_operator_component_status, https://docs.tigera.io/calico/latest/reference/installation/api). Available should be 1, Degraded and Progressing 0 (Progressing 1 briefly during upgrades).

panels.title: Reconcile errors by controller
panels.description: Errors per controller of the operator (controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total, https://book.kubebuilder.io/reference/metrics-reference). Persistent errors on one controller mean it cannot converge that component (see operator logs).

panels.title: Operator-managed TLS certificates: days left
panels.description: Days until each internal certificate the operator issues expires (tigera_operator_tls_certificate_expiry_timestamp_seconds: typha/node mTLS, webhooks, goldmane, whisker). The operator renews them; a value falling under 30 days means renewal is not happening.
